kind: Strategic Planner · The Vallmer Pack story, part 2
title: Vallmer Pack AG, the 2027 plan
subtitle: Three scenarios, sixty days of risk and a year in four gates
note: Vallmer Pack AG is an invented name for an example company: a Swiss maker of packaging machines for food and pharmaceutical factories, selling mostly in Germany and the euro area and some in the United States. Part 1 was its morning read; this part plans its year. Every finding is an Antevo engine's answer on the date shown; where an engine named a company, the page describes it instead. The company's details stayed with the assistant; the research question went to Antevo without its name. The scenarios, gates and measures are the assistant's options to consider, not advice.

thesis.label: The plan in one paragraph
thesis.text: Plan 2027 on the base case the strategy desk leans to, a managed reflation: the European Central Bank peaks around 3.0 to 3.25%, the franc stays between 0.90 and 0.93 to the euro and the 15% US tariff arrangement holds. Build the year so the stress case cannot break it. Commit now to what pays in every scenario: German orders, a service and retrofit line, and a second source for components. Stage what pays in only one: new capacity and a US hub. Hedge the franc in rolling twelve-month tranches rather than one block. Each large decision waits for its own signpost: the Swiss National Bank on 10 December, the ECB on 22 January, two to three German purchasing surveys above 53, a permanent US tariff deal. Meanwhile the radar itself has moved: in October its risks sat mostly in rates and government debt; in November AI funding and geopolitics caught up, and the trade-war risk is rising again.

tries.label: Three scenarios for 2027
tries.source: Antevo Research, strategy desk, 25 Nov 2026. The desk leans to the base case, with a stress tail.

items.name: Base case: managed reflation
evidence: The ECB peaks around 3.0 to 3.25%; the Swiss National Bank reaches 0.5% by mid-2027
EUR/CHF between 0.90 and 0.93; the US–Swiss 15% arrangement holds
Signposts: the ECB on 22 January 2027, German purchasing surveys above 53 through the first quarter, the SNB on 10 December

items.name: Upside: disinflation
evidence: Brent below 75 dollars for two months
An EU–US tariff freeze before the G7 in June 2027
German business expectations (Ifo) above 95 by February

items.name: Stress: a stagflation trap
evidence: The ECB at 3.5% or more; the French spread above 150 basis points before the election in the second quarter of 2027
EUR/CHF below 0.89
New US tariffs on EU goods; Swiss core inflation above 1.0%

plan.label: 2027 in four stages, each with a gate

items.title: Set the year
do: After the SNB on 10 December, hedge the first twelve-month tranche of euro income
Qualify a second source for Asian components; keep volumes small
File the service line's name, Vallmer Retrofit, and watch it
Hold multi-year price commitments until the first-quarter energy figures
Read the ECB on 22 January against the three scenarios
items.gate: The SNB and ECB decisions are read and the scenario lean is confirmed or changed in writing

items.title: Win Germany's orders
do: Put sales effort behind German food and pharmaceutical plants while demand is strong
Launch the retrofit and service offer to the installed base: revenue that holds in every scenario
Prepare the capacity case, but do not commit it
Refinance the bank loan while credit markets stay calm
items.gate: Two to three German purchasing surveys in a row above 53, and the order book confirms it

items.title: Commit or hold
do: If the gate held, commit the capacity expansion in steps
Watch the French spread into the election
Decide the US service hub once a permanent tariff deal is published, expected around mid-2027
Move second-source volumes up if supply-chain stress stays high
items.gate: A permanent US tariff arrangement is published, or the hub stays a plan

items.title: Lock in 2028
do: Set multi-year prices on the year's energy and franc readings
Roll the hedges forward a tranche
Rewrite the scenarios for 2028 from the radar's last sixty days
items.gate: The 2028 scenarios are written and every signpost has an owner

risks.label: The risk register, from the radar

items.risk: New tariffs on the largest trading partners · rising · first seen 10 March
items.trigger: Publication of tariff rates and dates; China's critical-material export rules; EU and Japanese responses
items.response: Keep the US hub staged; price US quotes with a tariff clause; second source outside the countries named

items.risk: AI-linked funding gets dearer · rising · 53 mornings since 14 March
items.trigger: Pricing of AI-linked bond and share sales; Tremor Watch high again with credit breaking
items.response: Refinance the bank loan early, while credit is the one calm family

items.risk: The Gulf truce frays · rising · 16 mornings since 3 July
items.trigger: Attacks on vessels near Hormuz; strikes on Saudi targets; Brent back above 95 dollars
items.response: Hold energy surcharges in quotes; delay fixed-price contracts

items.risk: Tariffs reach spring prices with no stockpile · stable
items.trigger: Core goods prices in the inflation figures; retailers' margin guidance; Pacific air cargo in December
items.response: Expect food customers to push back on capital spending in the spring; lead with retrofit

items.risk: A firm inflation figure restores rate-rise bets · stable · 63 mornings since 14 March
items.trigger: Two- and five-year Treasury yields after the figure; Fed speakers before December
items.response: Fix the loan rate rather than float it

items.risk: The franc breaks out of its range
items.trigger: EUR/CHF below 0.89, the stress line; the franc against the dollar already moving apart from Asian and US equities
items.response: Tranches, not one block; move more costs into euros

items.k: Tremor Watch status and how many times a normal week
items.why: High again with credit breaking closes the refinancing window
The stress case's line for margins on euro sales
The capacity gate: two to three readings in a row
Below 75 for two months is the upside; above 95 is the Gulf risk firing
Above it, the SNB rises faster and the stress case gains

items.k: The French spread against 150 basis points
items.why: The euro area's stress line before the election
When it stays high, second-source volumes move up

items.k: Radar risks rising, week by week
items.why: A rising count is the first sign the lean is changing

sections.title: The radar over sixty days
sections.so_what: A year planned on October's radar would have hedged the bond market and missed AI funding: refinancing now sits beside the franc as a first-quarter decision.
evidence: 58 mornings from 26 September to 25 November, 44 distinct risks
To 25 October: 52 of 140 entries on rates and government debt, 27 on geopolitics, 14 on AI concentration
From 26 October: 43 of 150 on rates, 33 on geopolitics, 32 on AI concentration: AI more than doubled
Most persistent: a US–Iran escalation on 33 mornings, last on 23 November; AI funding strain on 29; trade war back since 15 November
Dropped off: euro-area government debt, last on 30 October; emerging-market currency stress, last on 13 November

The regime read went from “A long end that no longer answers to oil” on 26 September, to “Politics sets the price” on 9 November, to “Rotation from AI suppliers to the shopper, with a tariff bill pending” today
sections.source: Antevo Executive Brief, risk radar and its evolution, 26 Sep – 25 Nov 2026

sections.title: How unsettled markets are
sections.so_what: The second spell of the year is cooling from its peak, but more pairs break each week: plan for a market that stays unsettled into 2027, and use the calm in credit while it lasts.
evidence: Elevated at 2.42 times a normal week in the week of 20 November, after High on 6 and 13 November (3.70x and 3.84x)
This year: High from 20 March to 15 May, peaking at 4.69x on 17 April; calm from June to mid-October
Breaking pairs per week: 10, 22, 30 and 31 over the last four weeks
Volatility 2.63x, commodities 2.48x and bonds 2.12x lead; credit is calm at 0.54x
Copper moves with US shares far more closely than its two-year norm: an input cost that now rises with a strong economy
The franc against the dollar has come apart from Japanese and US industrial shares since 13 November
sections.source: Antevo Tremor Watch, weeks to 20 Nov 2026 (provisional: 697 of 753 pairs read)

sections.title: The business board
sections.so_what: Germany is the opening the base case needs, and the tariff bill is the reason to keep the US staged.
evidence: German manufacturing and composite surveys stood at 55 in November, well above forecasts; France contracted
German business sentiment rose to 90.6 from 90.1
Higher US tariffs on China, the EU, Japan, South Korea and a dozen more are reported for this week; rates and dates not yet published
China's pause on its mineral export curbs runs until January
sections.source: Antevo Strategy Radar, business board, 25 Nov 2026

sections.title: Supply chains
sections.so_what: Qualify the second source now, while volumes can stay small: in the desk's words, dual-source now and defer the volumes.
evidence: Supply-chain stress at 79 of 100, read as critical, up from 62 on 26 October
Energy flows swing widely day to day: between 46 and 100 over the month, 64 today
Global trade activity flat, around 50
The index's own confidence is moderate: read the direction, not the decimal
sections.source: Antevo Executive Brief, indices, 26 Oct – 25 Nov 2026

sections.title: Decisions that wait for a signpost
sections.so_what: None of these has to be made in December, and each one costs more if it is made before its signpost.
evidence: Capacity expansion: wait for two or three German surveys above 53
US localisation: wait for a permanent tariff deal, around mid-2027
Asian components: dual-source now, defer the volumes
The franc: hedge in rolling twelve-month tranches until after the SNB
Multi-year prices: not before the first-quarter energy figures

sections.title: Names and the register
sections.so_what: Name the service line before it launches, and check every partner on the register before signing.
evidence: Vallmer Retrofit and Vallmer Uptime: no near marks in classes 7, 37 and 42, no Swiss company under either name, domains appear unregistered
Vallmer Care: one loosely similar mark, filed in the UK in an unrelated class

The Swiss register finds only two small limited companies with “packaging machines” in their names, in Graubünden and Thurgau: the field trades under its founders' names, so search partners by name, not by product
sections.source: Antevo Trademark and Antevo Companies, 25 Nov 2026

sections.title: The calendar
sections.so_what: Every signpost in the plan has a date: put them in the board's calendar, not in a drawer.
evidence: This week: US core inflation (25 Nov), French inflation (27 Nov), China's and Germany's November data (30 Nov)
1 December: euro-area inflation, consensus 4.3%; 4 December: US payrolls
10 December: the Swiss National Bank
22 January 2027: the ECB; the second quarter: the French election; June: the G7
sections.source: Antevo Executive Brief, catalysts, to 4 Dec 2026; later dates from the strategy desk

items.do: Write the three scenarios and the lean into the board pack
items.why: A plan built on one forecast breaks on the first surprise; three scenarios with signposts tell the board what would change the plan.

items.do: Read the SNB on 10 December, then place the first hedge tranche
items.why: The desk's advice is tranches until after the decision, not before.

items.do: File Vallmer Retrofit and watch it
items.why: The screen is clear today; a filing protects it, and a watch catches the next close mark.

items.do: Set up the early-warning dashboard and read it every Monday
items.why: The gates only work if someone looks: Tremor Watch weekly, the radar daily.

items.do: Check each second-source candidate on the register
items.why: Who they are, where they sit and who signs for them, from the public record.

links.text: The board shows German demand at its strongest in years, and the desk's base case needs it to last: the opening is real, but capacity waits for two or three readings in a row.
AI funding strain is on the radar on 29 of 58 mornings while credit is the one calm family in Tremor: refinance in the first quarter, while that still holds.
The franc has come apart from equities and the stress case draws its line at 0.89: hedge in tranches, so no single date decides the year's margin.
Supply-chain stress is critical and rising, and the desk says dual-source now: qualify the second source in December, buy the volumes later.
The service line's name is clear and the field does not trade under its product: name the line first, then check every partner by name.

watch: The published scope and start date of the US tariffs
The Swiss National Bank on 10 December 2026
Tremor Watch each Friday: whether credit starts to break
German purchasing surveys in January, February and March
disclaimer: From Antevo answers, each dated, and the public record. The scenarios are a desk's view, not a forecast, and the plan is options to consider. A trademark screen is not clearance. Not legal, tax or investment advice.
